title: Compute mean BCa acceleration without quadratic jackknife samples
body:
### Related Issues/PRs Relates to #26396, which introduced paired evaluation comparisons. ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? The BCa interval for the mean currently uses SciPy's generic jackknife. For N paired rows, that constructs and reduces N leave-one-out samples, adding quadratic work beyond the bootstrap resampling. For the mean, the jackknife influence values are proportional to each observation minus the sample mean. Compute the acceleration from those centered second and third moments in linear time. Normalize the deviations before taking powers, retain SciPy's mid-rank bias correction, and apply the same BCa quantile adjustment to the original 10,000 seeded bootstrap means. The seed, resample count, batching, confidence level, and percentile fallback remain unchanged. An undefined BCa interval reuses the percentile interval from the same bootstrap distribution. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests The 20 new numerical controls and the real constant-sample fallback control all pass on the original implementation. After this optimization, the complete comparison module plus the new controls pass: **78 tests**. The controls compare directly with native SciPy BCa jackknife intervals for small, normal, skewed, tied, binary, and negative-stride samples at three confidence levels. They also exercise the paired-comparison entry point and verify that inputs are unchanged. The fallback test uses actual undefined acceleration instead of a mocked bootstrap return. Local CPU timings, with one warmup and five timed repetitions per implementation and sample size, using the same lognormal data, 10,000 resamples, NumPy 2.5.4, and SciPy 1.18.1: | Paired rows | Original median | New median | | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1,000 | 35.15 ms | 32.42 ms | | 10,000 | 451.15 ms | 273.31 ms | | 25,000 | 1,963.62 ms | 760.50 ms | The largest bound difference in these benchmark cases is 1.56e-15. These are local confidence-interval timings, not end-to-end model or training measurements. The 10,000-by-N resampling cost remains. Ruff 0.16.8, Clint, character normalization, and `git diff --check` pass. The full MLflow suite and other SciPy versions were not run. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] Yes. Reduce the jackknife overhead of mean confidence intervals when comparing larger evaluation runs. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/evaluation`: MLflow model evaluation features, evaluation metrics, and evaluation workflows #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/none` - No description will be included. The PR will be mentioned only by the PR number in the "Small Bugfixes and Documentation Updates" section #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release?
What is a minor/patch release? - Minor release: a release that increments the second part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0). Minor releases are expected to contain larger changes, such as new features and improvements. Non-critical bug fixes and doc updates can be included as well. By default, your PR should target the next minor release. - Patch release: a release that increments the third part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1). Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low.
- [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release
